# Proxy Advisor Reliance

This letter asks the Commission to withdraw the proposed amendment to Rule 14a-2(b)(9), because the
amendment would raise the cost of advice without improving its accuracy.

Funds that subscribe to ISS vote with its recommendation on 92 percent of contested items, against
71 percent for funds that do not subscribe (Table 2). The gap is widest for small fund families,
which lack the staff to research each ballot item and buy the recommendation instead.

That reliance is a rational response to cost, not a failure of diligence. A fund family with three
analysts and four thousand ballot items a year cannot do otherwise, and a rule that raises the price
of advice will push those families toward voting with management by default.
